subject.title: fix(auth): bind OAuth and sessions to immutable identity

question: May this security hardening intentionally invalidate all existing email-owned sessions, durable records, and email-configured administrators, or must the release include a controlled legacy-owner recovery path?
rationale: The branch intentionally chooses a user-visible authorization and data-ownership migration policy; tests can prove either implementation, but cannot decide the acceptable recovery guarantee for deployed users.

options.title: Add controlled migration and recovery
options.body: Preserve the immutable-account destination while allowing verified owners or operators to migrate eligible legacy email-owned records with focused upgrade tests.

options.title: Accept immediate fail-closed invalidation
options.body: Land the strict rejection only if maintainers explicitly accept operator-led recreation or migration for every affected user and administrator.

options.title: Narrow to browser callback binding
options.body: Land or split out the OAuth browser-binding hardening while deferring durable identity migration until its recovery contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Add controlled migration and recovery
recommendation.body: Preserve the immutable-account destination while allowing verified owners or operators to migrate eligible legacy email-owned records with focused upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository-level authorization and upgrade policy needs a current project owner because individual historical ownership could not be established confidently.
